scripts.//spike-filter: The '!@spike/*' filter EXCLUDES the @spike/* DEV-ONLY fixtures under examples/ (dev-server, the synthetic stream/agent packs) from CI build/test/typecheck. The @rayspec/local-boot spec-driven boot wrapper is a @rayspec/* member and IS covered by CI.
scripts.//test: `--continue` keeps turbo running every package's test task after one fails, so a failure in one package cannot hide the results of the packages scheduled after it; turbo still exits non-zero when any task failed. `--concurrency=1` serializes turbo's package-level test tasks (one package's vitest at a time). WHY: `@rayspec/durable-dbos` + `@rayspec/server` are the only two packages that boot a REAL DBOS engine (DBOS.launch) and, run concurrently against the one shared local Postgres, cause catalog/pool pressure (deadlocks, CREATE/DROP-DATABASE lock races); separately, `@rayspec/cli`'s gen-handler typecheck test writes throwaway files into packages/kernel/platform/src and a concurrent `tsc -b` of platform/api-auth globs them mid-delete (TS6053). Serializing the turbo task graph removes both cross-package races. NOT MASKING A PROD BUG: this is a TEST-HARNESS artifact of N throwaway DBs + two engine-booting packages sharing ONE local Postgres; prod uses ONE app DB + ONE sys DB. Intra-package parallelism is unchanged (each vitest config still controls its own files); isolated `pnpm --filter X test` runs are unaffected (no `--concurrency` there). build/typecheck untouched. (Companion fix: `packages/app/cli/vitest.config.ts` raises the cli testTimeout to 60s so `cli/index.test.ts`'s in-process `plan` cold-start cannot trip the 5000ms default under full-suite CPU load. No wall-clock grace dependency remains: every suite that exercises the refresh grace window drives the injected clock the service also stamps `rotatedAt` from — `auth.test.ts`'s reuse-detection tests always did, and `org-selection-persistence.test.ts`'s ROTATED-cookie switch test now does too, so its rotate→switch hop no longer races the 30ms budget under load.)

scripts.//release: scripts/publish.mjs is the ONLY sanctioned path to npm: it transiently stamps the release version (DERIVED from this manifest's `version`; --version only asserts it) + flips private:false + ensures files:['dist'] for the CLI runtime closure, then ALWAYS restores the committed tree (private:true stays the accidental-publish guard). `release:tarballs` and `release:dry-run` are no-write proofs; a real registry write is `node scripts/publish.mjs --publish --yes-really-publish` with RAYSPEC_ALLOW_PUBLISH=1 and `--from` the tested tarballs, run by the manually dispatched release workflow with npm provenance or by the owner from a terminal, where npm can ask for the second factor (docs/releasing.md describes both). Requires `pnpm build` first. `release:candidate` builds a release candidate (tarballs, identity, SBOM, image, release manifest) under a transient pre-release version; `release:manifest` generates, signs and verifies the release manifest and the release evidence.
scripts.//release-identity: scripts/release-identity.mjs emits the RELEASE IDENTITY MANIFEST — the artifact that maps the published closure back to the commit it was built from (version, source commit + worktree state, per-package tarball integrity and unpacked file-list digest, the three schema artifacts, the lockfile and dependency-SBOM digests, the Node/pnpm requirements, the tag and the build workflow run). It is not signed itself: the signed release manifest (scripts/release-manifest.mjs) records its SHA-256. scripts/release-candidate.mjs runs steps 1 to 4 below for a candidate (stamped) and, with --release, for the release in the release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml, docs/releasing.md), which then publishes the tested tarballs themselves (`publish.mjs --publish --from`). By hand, a release run is: (1) `pnpm build` and `rm -f packages/app/rayspec/rayspec-release-identity.json` — the manifest is gitignored and listed in the launcher's `files`, so a manifest left by the PREVIOUS release run would be packed into this release's launcher tarball, which no manifest generated for this release can match (packing is not byte-reproducible); step 3 refuses in that case rather than emitting an unverifiable manifest; (2) `node scripts/publish.mjs --pack --out release/v<version>`; (3) `pnpm release:identity --tarballs release/v<version>` — writes packages/app/rayspec/rayspec-release-identity.json, which the publish in step 5 packs into the launcher tarball it uploads; (4) `pnpm release:identity-verify --tarballs release/v<version>` — must print 0 failures; (5) publish per the //release note; (6) attach the manifest AND the tarballs it pins to the GitHub release: `gh release upload v<version> packages/app/rayspec/rayspec-release-identity.json release/v<version>/*.tgz`. Step 6 is the release-asset half of the manifest's reachability; the launcher tarball is the installed-package half.
